notes:

items.title: Councillor C. Huinink Notice of Motion, Re: Mobility Plus Setting the Target for Undelivered Trips
Councillor C. Huinink Notice of Motion, Re: Faster Software Upgrade for Mobility Plus
notes:
C. Huinink introduced the motion, noting that the goal is to procure better software in order to transport more people to where they need to go. C. Huinink stated that there is no budgetary ask at this time, but there may be an ask in 2025. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, D. Spooner confirmed that MobilityPlus is fully operated through GRT and the software is used by the Region.

J. Liggett joined the meeting at 10:57 am.

items.title: Councillor N. Salonen Notice of Motion, Re: Oxford Road 5
notes:
N. Salonen joined the meeting at 11:00 am.

N. Salonen introduced the motion, sharing that Township of Wilmot staff have been working to have this road uploaded to the Region for over 3 years, and that Regional transportation staff are in support of the upload, with there being some financial implications. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, Rod Regier, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services, noted that there is a road assumption policy, which staff are currently reviewing and planning to bring a report to Council in March 2024. R. Regier noted that that would be the right time to have a conversation regarding Oxford Road 5, as there are implications regarding the policy.

items.title: Councillor N. Salonen Notice of Motion, Re: Waste Management Rebate for Townhome Complexes
notes:
N. Salonen introduced the motion, sharing that the ask is for these complexes to be separate from multi residential buildings and for staff to bring back information as to the implications of re-implementing the waste management rebate for these townhome complexes. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering and Environmental Services, shared that the rebate program was removed from the budget in 2021, resulting in a reduction of 1.9 million dollars or approximately $36/year per townhouse or unit. J. Rose confirmed that staff are looking to include a multi residential study into the waste management master plan.

motions.item_title: TSD-TRS-24-002, GRT Universal Transit Pass 2024 Program Updates
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo: Enter into an agreement with Conestoga Students Incorporated and Conestoga College to implement a universal transit pass (U-Pass) program for an initial term ending August 31, 2027 with a mutual option to renew, in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024; Amend and extend the existing U-Pass agreements with the Wilfrid Laurier University Students Union (WLUSU) and Wilfrid Laurier University, the Wilfrid Laurier University Graduate Students Association (WLU GSA) and Wilfrid Laurier University, the Waterloo Undergraduate Students Association (WUSA), the University of Waterloo Graduate Students Association (UW GSA), and the English Language Institute at Renison University College (Renison ELI), for a term ending August 31, 2027 with a mutual option to renew, in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024; and Approve an interim U-Pass Fee Schedule and associated annual price increases for the 2025/2026 Academic Year and 2026/2027 Academic Year for all U-Pass programs, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo:

  1. Enter into an agreement with Conestoga Students Incorporated and Conestoga College to implement a universal transit pass (U-Pass) program for an initial term ending August 31, 2027 with a mutual option to renew, in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024;
  2. Amend and extend the existing U-Pass agreements with the Wilfrid Laurier University Students Union (WLUSU) and Wilfrid Laurier University, the Wilfrid Laurier University Graduate Students Association (WLU GSA) and Wilfrid Laurier University, the Waterloo Undergraduate Students Association (WUSA), the University of Waterloo Graduate Students Association (UW GSA), and the English Language Institute at Renison University College (Renison ELI), for a term ending August 31, 2027 with a mutual option to renew, in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024; and
  3. Approve an interim U-Pass Fee Schedule and associated annual price increases for the 2025/2026 Academic Year and 2026/2027 Academic Year for all U-Pass programs, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024.

motions.item_title: EES-DCS-24-001, Conestoga College Transit Hub - Approval of Design Concept

motions.text_html:

  1. Approve the Recommended Design Concept for the Conestoga College Transit Hub as set out in Appendix A; and

     

  2. Increase the Consulting Services Agreement with Arcadis Professional Services (Canada) Inc. to provide engineering consulting for detailed design, contract administration, and site inspection services for the proposed Conestoga College Transit Hub in the City of Kitchener by $357,000 for a revised upset limit total of $590,100 plus applicable taxes, with construction contract administration and inspection to be paid on a time basis.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. Huinink Notice of Motion, Re: Mobility Plus Setting the Target for Undelivered Trips
motions.text: Whereas 6% of the current transit operating budget is allocated to Mobility Plus; and Whereas the current rate of undelivered trips on Mobility Plus is 5%, and has been as high as 15% historically; Therefore be it resolved that the target rate for undelivered trips will be 2.5% for 2024; and That staff continue to report quarterly on the rate of undelivered trips (previously called “unaccommodated trips”).
motions.text_html:
Whereas 6% of the current transit operating budget is allocated to Mobility Plus; and 

Whereas the current rate of undelivered trips on Mobility Plus is 5%, and has been as high as 15% historically;

Therefore be it resolved that the target rate for undelivered trips will be 2.5% for 2024; and

That staff continue to report quarterly on the rate of undelivered trips (previously called “unaccommodated trips”).

motions.item_title: Councillor C. Huinink Notice of Motion, Re: Faster Software Upgrade for Mobility Plus
motions.text: Whereas Mobility Plus’ total capacity is determined by resources (buses and operators), and the ability to optimize and group trips across the region; and Whereas staff are exploring an upgrade to the Mobility Plus booking and scheduling software; Therefore be it resolved that staff report back in-year, with the necessary operating and capital investments to accelerate the implementation of the Mobility Plus scheduling software upgrade and improve the optimization and grouping of trips.
motions.text_html:
Whereas Mobility Plus’ total capacity is determined by resources (buses and operators), and the ability to optimize and group trips across the region; and 

Whereas staff are exploring an upgrade to the Mobility Plus booking and scheduling software;

Therefore be it resolved that staff report back in-year, with the necessary operating and capital investments to accelerate the implementation of the Mobility Plus scheduling software upgrade and improve the optimization and grouping of trips.

motions.item_title: Councillor N. Salonen Notice of Motion, Re: Waste Management Rebate for Townhome Complexes
motions.text: Whereas one of the key strategic pillars of council is Equitable Services; and Whereas legislatively the Region of Waterloo is not required to provide waste collection to multi- residential buildings over 6 units as they are deemed commercial; and Whereas townhome complexes are not deemed commercial and as such are the responsibility of the Region to provide waste removal services, yet some complexes do not receive service because they do not meet the truck access criteria; and Whereas in complexes where truck access criteria are not met, the Region had commenting authority on the plan of subdivisions prior to these complexes being built, and the Region did not make comment on complexes with no through roads in context of waste removal truck access; Therefore, be it resolved that the Committee direct staff to bring a report that provides further information on the implications of re-implementing the waste management rebate for townhome complexes that do not meet the truck access criteria to a Planning and Works Committee meeting, no later than April 9, 2024.
motions.text_html:
Whereas one of the key strategic pillars of council is Equitable Services; and

Whereas legislatively the Region of Waterloo is not required to provide waste collection to multi- residential buildings over 6 units as they are deemed commercial; and

Whereas townhome complexes are not deemed commercial and as such are the responsibility of the Region to provide waste removal services, yet some complexes do not receive service because they do not meet the truck access criteria; and

Whereas in complexes where truck access criteria are not met, the Region had commenting authority on the plan of subdivisions prior to these complexes being built, and the Region did not make comment on complexes with no through roads in context of waste removal truck access;

Therefore, be it resolved that the Committee direct staff to bring a report that provides further information on the implications of re-implementing the waste management rebate for townhome complexes that do not meet the truck access criteria to a Planning and Works Committee meeting, no later than April 9, 2024.
